Scope and principles Planwise Lab is an English-language planning and learning site for students, freelancers, and small teams. The first release contains four deterministic tools: project planning, capacity planning, decision comparison, and study scheduling. The architecture separates public presentation, interactive workspace, pure calculation engines, optional authenticated persistence, and shared validation/contracts. Calculation correctness must not depend on authentication, persistence, browser storage, network access, or wall-clock time. Anonymous calculation is the primary path. Optional private cloud persistence is secondary and must never be required for calculation. ## 2. Public/private boundary Public, crawlable surfaces include tool landing pages, methodology/explanatory content, reviewed guides, public examples without private data, and publisher/legal pages once real owner information exists. Private/non-indexable surfaces include saved projects, authenticated workspace records, persisted private inputs/outputs, account/session data, server diagnostics, and unapproved private imports. Robots/canonical controls are defense-in-depth only; authorization is server-side. Anonymous workspaces remain in browser memory until an explicit save/export action. There is no implicit server upload when a calculation runs. ## 3. Recommended stack and corrected compatibility evidence ### Proposed baseline
Layer Recommendation Evidence / status
Framework Next.js 16.3.4, App Router Current 16.3 patch identified in package registry; Next.js official installation docs specify Node \>=20.9 and manual installation with `next`, `react`, and `react-dom`.
UI runtime React 19.3.0 + react-dom 19.3.0 React official versions page lists 19.3.0 as released 2026-09-09; react-dom 19.3.0 is published.
Language TypeScript 6.0.x, subject to bootstrap validation Next.js official docs require TypeScript \>=5.1.0; exact TS 6.0 integration with the selected dependency lock is not yet proven.
Runtime Node.js 24 LTS Meets Next.js documented minimum of 20.9; exact Node/Next native-module matrix remains a bootstrap check.
Styling Tailwind CSS, version pinned during bootstrap Next.js official create-next-app flow supports Tailwind; exact dependency version is not frozen here.
Validation Zod or equivalent runtime schema library Boundary-validation requirement; exact package/version remains an implementation decision.
Persistence Supabase PostgreSQL + Auth, optional Retained from approved architecture proposal; private persistence only.
SSR auth adapter `@supabase/ssr` Retained from existing Supabase recommendation; exact version remains an implementation-time dependency decision.
### What is verified, and what is not The previous revision incorrectly treated version existence as proof of a compatible dependency combination. This revision does **not** claim that an exact lockfile has been compatibility-tested. Verified from authoritative/current sources: - Next.js official installation documentation states a minimum Node.js version of 20.9, supports TypeScript with a minimum of 5.1.0, and documents installation of `next`, `react`, and `react-dom`. citeturn3search0 - Next.js published package metadata identifies the 16.3.x line, with 16.3.4 currently published. citeturn0search6 - React official documentation identifies 19.3 as the latest React version and records React 19.3.0 as released September 9, 2026. citeturn0search1turn0search0 - `react-dom` 19.3.0 is published and is intended to be paired with React. citeturn0search9 **Compatibility status: UNVERIFIED, not PASS.** Existence, minimum runtime requirements, and official installation guidance are established, but the repository has not yet run a clean dependency-resolution/build against the exact proposed versions. No compatibility test is being represented as performed. ### Bounded reproducible bootstrap validation Before implementation pins versions, the frontend owner should use a clean temporary workspace and record the actual output of: 1. `npm view next@16.3.4 engines peerDependencies --json` 2. `npm view react@19.3.0 version --json` 3. `npm view react-dom@19.3.0 version --json` 4. `npm view typescript@6.0.x version --json` 5. `npm install next@16.3.4 react@19.3.0 react-dom@19.3.0 typescript@6.0.x --package-lock-only` 6. `npm ls next react react-dom typescript --all` 7. `npm run build` after a minimal App Router bootstrap using the resolved lockfile. Acceptance for stack compatibility is: peer requirements resolve without overrides/legacy-peer-deps; the lockfile resolves one intended React/React-DOM pair; the selected Node LTS runs the build; and the build completes without dependency-resolution or runtime-version errors. If any check fails, revise the version set rather than forcing installation. ## 4. Exact path ownership and exclusions The ownership table below mirrors the current task reservations and explicit path boundaries. It is an ownership map, not permission to implement outside the assigned issue.
Role Exact owned/allowed paths relevant to architecture Explicit exclusions / notes
Manager `coordination/`; integration transfer evidence; manager-owned workflow files Owns inboxes, master plan, decisions and integration log. Does not silently edit worker deliverables.
Architect `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`; own status/outbox/checkpoint/handoff Issue #21 is limited to `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` plus the architect's own communication/checkpoint files. No API/schema/contracts/application implementation.
Designer `docs/UI_SPEC.md`; `docs/design/`; `content/`; `docs/EDITORIAL_REVIEW.md` Designer owns editorial/content work under current reservations. No frontend application implementation.
Frontend `apps/web/` **excluding** `apps/web/src/app/api/` and `apps/web/src/server/`; `package.json`; `package-lock.json`; `tsconfig.json`; `tests/frontend/` Frontend owns root build configuration. Backend API/server paths are excluded. Engine/contracts are not frontend-owned.
Backend `packages/engine/`; `apps/web/src/app/api/`; `apps/web/src/server/`; `supabase/`; `tests/backend/` Backend implementation must consume approved contracts. No ownership of frontend UI or editorial content.
QA `tests/e2e/`; `tests/accessibility/`; `docs/QA_REPORT.md`; `docs/BUGS.md` QA owns end-to-end/accessibility verification paths, not product implementation.
Security/DevOps `.github/`; `docs/SECURITY_REVIEW.md`; `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`; `docs/ADSENSE_READINESS.md`; security configuration with manager path reservation Security-sensitive changes require this role's review. No production/paid activation is implied.
Cross-cutting communication rule: every worker may update only its own status/outbox/checkpoint/handoff. Manager owns role inboxes and coordination records. No role reservation by itself authorizes implementation. ## 5. Module boundaries Proposed application structure: ```plain text apps/web/ src/app/ Next.js routes and public/workspace pages src/components/ accessible presentation src/features/ tool-specific UI adapters src/lib/browser/ browser persistence/import/export src/lib/auth/ auth adapters src/server/ authenticated persistence/application services packages/engine/ project/ planning and critical-path calculations capacity/ capacity and overload calculations decision/ decision comparison and sensitivity study/ study scheduling and impossible-schedule reporting shared/ deterministic date/workday utilities packages/contracts/ versioned inputs/outputs, schemas, errors, import/export envelopes content/guides/ reviewed original guides ``` The pure engine must not import Next.js, React, browser APIs, HTTP clients, Supabase, or authentication libraries. ## 6. Four-tool calculation boundaries ### Project planning Explicit calendar/workday mode; duplicate or missing IDs invalid; negative duration invalid; zero duration only if later contract permits milestones; cycles are domain errors; deterministic topological ordering; critical path/float only after acyclic validation; PERT uses `(optimistic + 4 * mostLikely + pessimistic) / 6` when selected; impossible constraints return structured impossible-schedule results. ### Capacity planning Explicit per-person availability and nonworking dates; allocation exceeding availability produces overload information; deadlines are not silently moved; equal allocation choices use deterministic stable tie-breaking; date/time semantics are explicit. ### Decision comparison Positive weights with explicit normalization; benefit/cost direction is explicit; missing values are not silently converted to zero; ties are first-class; zero-range normalization is defined; invalid/non-finite numeric inputs are rejected; sensitivity preserves ties/ranges rather than false precision. ### Study scheduling Explicit topics, effort, available slots, and deadlines; review intervals are a declared calculation policy rather than a learning guarantee; impossible schedules identify limiting constraints; edited sessions have an explicit later contract for preservation/regeneration; deterministic tie-breaking is required. ## 7. Error/result model Validation errors, domain errors, impossible schedules, warnings, and valid ties are separate structured outcomes. UI text must not be the source of truth for detecting these states. ## 8. Determinism and dates Engines receive explicit reference dates and timezone/calendar semantics. They never read the current clock implicitly. Intermediate numerical precision is retained; presentation rounding occurs at the UI boundary unless a mathematical method explicitly requires otherwise. ## 9. Anonymous data flow ```plain text input -> boundary validation -> pure engine -> deterministic result -> UI explanation/export ``` No server call is required for anonymous calculation. ## 10. Private persistence flow ```plain text authenticated request -> session validation -> ownership check -> validated payload -> persistence -> response ``` Every private read/write is authorized server-side. Cross-user access is denied. Optimistic concurrency and import-size limits are required implementation constraints. ## 11. Import/export boundary Import is untrusted input. It must be size-limited, schema-validated, version-aware, and rejected on malformed/unsupported envelopes. Import must not execute arbitrary code. Export is a deterministic representation of validated workspace state. ## 12. Authentication/session boundary Authentication is only required for private cloud persistence. Session handling remains server-aware; browser code receives only the minimum state needed by the UI. No service-role or database credentials may enter client bundles. Supabase RLS is defense-in-depth, not a substitute for application authorization checks. ## 13. Indexing and privacy Private routes and data are non-indexable, but robots controls are not authorization. Public pages must not leak identifiers, saved workspace data, diagnostics, or authenticated state into crawlable HTML or metadata. ## 14. Accessibility and presentation boundary Public and interactive pages are frontend responsibilities; the engine returns structured data so the UI can provide charts plus tabular equivalents, keyboard navigation, meaningful errors, and screen-reader-friendly explanations. Accessibility evidence is owned under the QA paths listed in Section 4. ## 15. Performance boundary The project targets responsive interaction with 200 tasks. Engine benchmarks should be independent of network/database latency. Browser performance must be measured separately on recorded benchmark hardware. The architecture does not treat lab performance as proof of field performance. ## 16. Security boundaries Threats requiring explicit review include XSS through imported/rendered content, malicious oversized imports, cross-user authorization failures, RLS misconfiguration, session leakage, dependency vulnerabilities, secrets in client bundles, and accidental indexing of private workspaces. Security review is required before contract freeze where security-sensitive decisions are affected. ## 17. Testing strategy Engines require unit/property tests, deterministic fixtures, cycle/tie/impossible-schedule cases, invalid-input cases, and a 200-task benchmark. Later browser work requires component/browser, keyboard, accessibility, import/export, persistence and end-to-end tests. Tests not yet run must be labeled not run. ## 18. Freeze and change policy This document is a proposal. API/schema/contracts remain unfrozen until reviewed PRs and a corresponding decision record freeze them. Version changes after bootstrap require dependency review. No worker may silently alter another role's contract or path ownership. ## 19. Architecture acceptance checklist - Four tools have explicit edge-case behavior: **specified**. - Anonymous calculation independent of persistence/auth: **specified**. - Private ownership/auth boundary: **specified**. - Exact path ownership and exclusions: **corrected in this revision**. - Stack versions identified: **specified**. - Stack compatibility evidence: **corrected to UNVERIFIED with reproducible validation plan**. - No unperformed compatibility/build check is represented as passed: **yes**. - Implementation authorized by this document: **no**. ## Revision evidence PR #22 requested two corrections: exact path ownership and honest stack-compatibility evidence. This revision addresses both without modifying the original Notion submission. Actual evidence available for this revision: - PR #22 state: open, `CHANGES_REQUESTED`, head `ccf944d400875ae81bd8dc8ef730420bdd7a8d81`. - PR #22 manager review explicitly identified the Section 14 ownership mismatch and unsupported compatibility claim. - Official Next.js installation requirements and React release/version evidence were rechecked on 2026-09-12. citeturn3search0turn0search1turn0search0 - No local worker Git branch/write operation was available for this submission, so `git diff --check`, lockfile resolution, `npm ls`, and application build were **not run**. They are therefore not claimed as passed. **Submission status:** READY_FOR_REVIEW. Manager transfer remains required. Security-devops review remains required for the proposal's security boundaries.
